claims.summary: Over any field, for a down-set X of {0,1}^N the associated graded algebra of the functions on X under the degree filtration is the face ring of X modulo the squares, with socle spanned by the facets; so it has a perfect graded pairing, the hypothesis of prop:frobenius-marked-separation, exactly when X has one facet (a standard computation). Product domains with one-hot coordinates are such down-sets, of socle dimension prod max(|A_j|-1,1), Gorenstein exactly when every |A_j|<=2; the hole-respecting assignments of the product pigeonhole system with m>=2 pigeons have no such pairing. Graded annihilation bounds domain killers from below: fE=0 on X gives lead(f)lead(E)=0 in the graded algebra, while a graded annihilator need not lift (x_[N] on the cube); on the cube both least degrees for monomial errors are the transversal number.
claims.assessment: Working proof of a standard computation, passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with a follow-up; the leading-form direction and the non-lifting example are its corrections.
claims.rationale: Shows marked Frobenius separation does not apply on the line's non-cube domain models and fixes the direction in which graded duality bears: a lower bound.
claims.next_action: Compute the top-part space of the functional pigeonhole closure and test the leading-form bound there.
